subject: Renewal conversation: flexible rate-smoothing + triggered credit proposal
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@orchid.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal timing + usage volatility — need options

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the trial support last quarter. We're lining up our renewal for early November but wanted to flag that our usage this summer was spikier than anticipated — 3 big model-driven bursts in July and August. The finance team is concerned about OOB charges and we want a clean renewal that reduces surprise overage risk while keeping a predictable unit price as we scale.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a renewal that blends a price-hold for the first 6 months with a stepdown credit mechanism if we fall below committed usage, plus the option to increase committed capacity mid-term without penalty? Also, invoice timing flexibility would help (quarterly invoicing vs monthly).

Attaching a short export of our Q3 usage to help you model.

Appreciate a couple of concrete options we can present to procurement next week.

Best,
Emma

[Attachment: Q3-usage-summary.csv]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@orchid.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + usage volatility — need options

Thanks Emma — useful data, appreciate the context.

High-level we can do two practical paths that balance predictability for you and capacity planning for us:

Option A — 12-month commit, increased commit discount:
- 12-month term with a 10% unit-price discount off list if you commit to a 25% uplift in monthly committed tokens
- Price hold for first 9 months
- Standard overage rates after commit

Option B — Flexible hold + triggered credits (recommended for volatility):
- 6-month price hold on current unit price, followed by a review
- Stepdown credits: if average usage over any 30-day window falls below 70% of committed capacity, Orchid receives a credit equal to 50% of the difference for that month (credit applied to next invoice)
- One mid-term commit increase allowed (no penalty) with a 30-day notice
- Option to switch to the 12-month uplift (Option A) at an agreed conversion discount schedule

We can also offer quarterly invoicing for your accounting team as a short-term accommodation.

I've attached a draft term sheet with the above laid out. If helpful, I can run an internal quick-impact on margin for Option B — wanted to loop Karthik/Monica now so we can align before you take an option to procurement.

Can we do a 30-minute call Thursday to walk this? If your procurement wants the exact credit formula we can put it into the amendment.

Thanks,
Ben

[Attachment: DraftTermSheet_v1.pdf]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Renewal timing + usage volatility — internal: proposed concession matrix

Internal — forwarding Orchid thread with usage export. High-level recommendation for tradeoffs we can make without breaking our forecast.

Recommended concession matrix (Option B base):
- Price hold: 6 months
- Stepdown credit trigger: avg 30-day usage < 70% of committed monthly tokens -> credit = 50% of shortfall value for that month (credit applied to next invoice)
- Mid-term commit increase: allowed once, effective after 30 days, no penalty and pro-rata pricing based on new commit
- Invoice cadence: quarterly invoicing (invoiced at start of quarter) with payment terms Net 45 (instead of Net 30) for this customer through the first renewal year

Impact notes: estimated revenue deferral from Net45 / quarterly moves ~ $45k cash timing shift; conservatively the credit exposure at current runrate ~ $60k over 12 months if usage drops persistently. Margin impact (estimate): ~4.2% on ARR for the first year under Option B.

Ask: please flag any regs/legal friction on Net45 or credit language and sign off on the credit cap. I'm proposing a cap: credits cannot exceed 20% of annual recurring contract value (ACV).

Attached simple P&L sensitivity model. I will surface this on the call with Emma if we get time.

Ben

[Attachment: ConcessionImpact_model.xlsx]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>

Ben — this looks reasonable. A few tweaks:
- Cap the monthly credit to the greater of (i) $10k or (ii) 20% of monthly ACV divided by 12 (keeps extremes bounded)
- Keep credit application to next invoice but require customer to acknowledge the credit terms in the amendment (prevents disputes)
- Approve Net45 for year one; ask finance to sign off on the cash cadence impact

Monica, please prep a short paragraph for the amendment that explains the trigger and cap in customer-friendly terms. If legal needs to update SOW wording we can route quickly — but avoid bespoke legal delays if we can get procurement to accept amendment language.

If that's fine I authorize Ben to send the consolidated Option B offer to Emma with the cap and Net45.

Karthik
